summary: Low end for masters, buses and drums: the band below a crossover (20–300 Hz, Linkwitz–Riley 24, minimum phase or linear phase) goes through a transient/sustain shaper (Punch and Sustain), Contrast (keep the strongest parts of the low end and pull the rest, or the reverse), Balance (the low band toward a set level against the mid band), Peak control (a soft clipper on the low band only) and mono below a frequency, then is added back to everything above the crossover, which is left alone. Delta (hear only what it changes) and a gain-match reading. Use it to tighten, focus or mono-ise the bass and kick of a mix or master.

parameters.name: Crossover
parameters.description: Where the low band ends (−6 dB here). Everything above it is left as it was

parameters.name: Phase
parameters.description: Minimum: the Linkwitz–Riley split, its only latency the lookahead. Linear: a linear-phase split on FIRs of 8192 taps (latency 96 ms at 48 kHz, reported and compensated), the band's phase untouched. Set it before playing

parameters.name: Punch
parameters.description: Gain on the onsets of the low band (kick, bass attack), 0.1 dB steps

parameters.name: Sustain
parameters.description: Gain on the body and tail of the low band, 0.1 dB steps

parameters.name: Speed
parameters.description: The followers' time constants for Punch and Sustain. Smooth: for sustained bass

parameters.name: Lookahead
parameters.description: The shaping's gains are worked out this long before the audio they act on, so Punch is already up at a kick's first peak. Minimum phase: the audio is delayed this long (the latency, reported and compensated). Linear phase: free (the FIR's latency is far longer)

parameters.name: Contrast
parameters.description: Gain from how far the low band is above or below its slow level (300 ms): +100 % keeps the strongest parts and pulls the rest (up to 12 dB), −100 % does the reverse, 0 leaves it. The band's energy is kept

parameters.name: Target
parameters.description: The level of the low band over the mid band (the band above the crossover up to 2 kHz) Balance moves toward, measured over 1 s

parameters.name: Balance
parameters.description: How much of the distance to Target is corrected (at most ±9 dB on the low band, moving slowly); 0 leaves the low band's level alone

parameters.name: Peak control
parameters.description: A soft clipper (a 6 dB knee, antiderivative anti-aliased) on the low band only: its peaks stay under Peak level, the rest of the sound is untouched

parameters.name: Peak level
parameters.description: Where the low band's peaks are held, dBFS (0.1 dB steps)

parameters.name: Mono
parameters.description: Makes the low band mono below Mono freq (the side signal is removed there)

parameters.name: Mono freq
parameters.description: Below this the low band's side signal is removed (a 4th-order Linkwitz–Riley high-pass on it, −6 dB here)

parameters.name: Output
parameters.description: Gain after the shaper, 0.1 dB steps (the editor's Match sets it from the gain-match reading)

parameters.name: Delta
parameters.description: Hear only what Low End changes: the output minus the input, delayed to match (gliding over 10 ms)

readings.description: Short-term loudness out − in (K-weighted, 3 s): what Output would have to take back for equal loudness
The low band's crest factor (peak over RMS) going in
The low band's crest factor going out: the change is what Punch, Contrast and Peak control did
The low band's level over the mid band's now (measured on the input, 1 s average)
The gain Balance is applying to the low band
How far the low band went over Peak level (0 when it stayed under, or Peak control is off)
The latency (0 in minimum phase), reported to NeoBuzz Live
